In 1848 shovels usually cost 25 cents, but now that Brannan owned them all, he charged 15 dollars for each shovel!
People were desperate for gold, and in only nine weeks, Brannan made $36,000 selling tools.
Over the next year, stories about rivers full of gold in California spread east.
People in the eastern United States were eager to mine gold, but there was no easy way to get to California.
Some people crossed the plains in covered wagons, and other people traveled by boat around South America.
Either way the trip took at least six months, and very few people survived.
Many hopeful miners traveled to California using wagons.
However, California is on the edge of the Nevada desert.
Many people would run out of water and die in the desert when they were so close to the end of their journey.
Californian businessmen decided to make money off this,
so they rode into the desert with large barrels of water and sold glasses of water for one dollar, five dollars,
and even one hundred dollars to thirsty travelers!
The biggest years of the Gold Rush were 1848 through 1850.
During those two years, people traveled to California from China, Mexico, Europe, and all over the United States to find gold.
This made California an international cultural center unlike any other place in the world.
Unfortunately of the 25,000 people who traveled to California to find gold, very few became rich.
In fact, most of the people who became rich during the Gold Rush never lifted a shovel.
The people who made the most money from the Gold Rush were those who took care of the miners.
There were very few women in California at this time, so the ones who were there made a lot of money by taking care of the men.
For example, one woman made $18,000 just by selling pies she baked in her oven.
Another woman charged eight dollars just to wash a dozen pieces of laundry, when in other states it cost only 25 cents.
Other women made dinner for twenty men every night and sold each plate of food for ten dollars!
In any other state, these prices would have been robbery, but in California the miners were desperate and paid the high prices.
Many men who left their homes to find gold in California also left their families behind.
"I'll be home in a year, and we'll be richer than you can dream," a man would promise his family as he left.
But with so many people in California, it became very difficult to find gold, and many men were not able to return to their families.
Women were scarce in California, and the men were lonely.
One man was able to find a bride in California, and when he got married, he charged men five dollars to come to the wedding to see his new wife.
The men were so desperate to see a woman's face that they happily paid five dollars each!
The story of the Gold Rush is a story of both riches and poverty.
Though many people didn't become rich, in the end they created a very rich state.
Today California celebrates its Gold Rush history in many ways—
one of which is San Francisco's football team, named the 49ers after the many gold miners who arrived in 1849.
Of course there may still be gold in that American River; no one really knows.

episodes.title: Frances Ann on the Oregon Trail

subtitle.text: Hi, my name is Frances Ann. Ma said you might be walking with us today.
I hope you aren’t eating dinner with us because we’re low on bacon.
"Frances Ann! Mind your manners!"
"Yes, Ma." That’s my mother. Up in front, driving the wagon, is my father.
His name is Lloyd Rollins, and he is taking us to Oregon to find gold.
"Hi, darlin’."
"Hi, Pa!" Pa says one day we’re going to strike gold and we’ll be rich.
Over there is my sister Josephine. She’s bossy, so I walk on this side of the wagon where she can’t tell me what to do.
That man with her is Ezra Meeker, but I think he’s crazy.
He loves the Oregon Trail, and I think he likes my sister.
Behind us is Henderson Luelling, and Pa says he really is crazy.
He’s bringing three wagons to Oregon, and two of them are full of fruit and nut trees!
Well, since we’ve got all day, I may as well tell you about where we’ve been. So listen closely.
In 1836 when my sister Josephine was born, Pa’s friend Marcus Whitman left to go to Oregon.
Pa wanted to go with him, but Ma said she wasn’t ready yet. Oregon was two thousand miles away.
On my seventh birthday, Pa said his girls were grown, and it was time to leave.
So here we are, going to Oregon in 1850.
Our trip began in Missouri.
We loaded up our wagon with a thousand pounds of bacon, coffee, flour, salt, and sugar, and got on a ferry to cross the Missouri River.
We jumped off at a town called Independence and waited for the grass to grow.
There were hundreds of wagons all over the town.
It was March then, and since grass doesn’t grow until April, we all had to wait.
If we left too early, our oxen would starve to death, and we’d be stuck.
Of course, if we left too late, we would freeze to death at the end of the trip.
It takes a long time to walk two thousand miles―almost six months.
So everybody had to wait for the perfect time to leave. Every day more wagons arrived.
There were so many that I could almost walk to town on the tops of them.
April finally came, the oxen ate the grass, and everyone left at once.
There was dust everywhere. Ma was worried that I might trip and fall under a wagon.
She said that if that happened I could lose my leg or even die, so I’ve been really careful.
Oh look, there’s another stove. Ma wanted to bring our stove to Oregon, but Pa said no because it was too heavy.
Ma cried. She said other women were bringing stoves, but he wouldn’t let her.
And now look, Pa was right. These people had too much stuff in their wagon, and they had to throw their stoves out.
Why? Well, because the stove was too heavy, and pulling it made the oxen tired.
These oxen aren’t as pretty as horses, or as fast, but they’re stronger.
Some people have mules because they are strong too, but they kick too much and don’t go when you tell them.
I wish I could ride the oxen, but Ma says it isn’t ladylike. I don’t mind getting my hands dirty.
I’m getting hungry. It must be dinnertime soon.
Every morning we get up with the sun at six o’clock.
Ma cooks bacon and bread, Pa ties the oxen to the wagon, and Josephine and I clean up.
We walk all morning and have a short lunch of bacon and bread.
Then we walk until the sun is just about down, and we have bacon and bread for dinner.
At night we have to make a circle with our wagons to keep our animals inside.
I collect buffalo chips so we can make a fire. What are they?
Why, you are silly! Buffalo chips are dried buffalo dung.
But don’t worry; they don’t smell bad and they make a nice fire.
After dinner we’ll crawl under the wagon to rest.
Sometimes Ma and Pa talk when they think I’m asleep.
Ma cries because she’s worried that we won’t make it to Oregon.
In some wagon trains, two out of every three people died of cholera.
Of course there are also lightning strikes and sometimes hail the size of apples.
People have run out of food, drowned in rivers, and even been hurt by accidental gunshots.
Ma worries about everything, but Pa says it will be worth it.
Pa says that one day we’ll be rich.
We’ll be so rich, he’ll name a place Josephine County, and hundreds of people will come to live there. I hope he’s right.
The Real Story
Though Frances Ann is a fictional character, some of the other people mentioned in this story actually made the journey across the Oregon Trail.
However, many details about their lives have been invented and changed in this telling of Frances Ann’s story.
Ezra Meeker loved the Oregon Trail so much that he traveled it four times.
Henderson Luelling was also a real person.
He arrived in Oregon with his family and many different kinds of trees (apple, cherry, pear, plum, and black walnut).
His orchards grew to be abundant. And because no one else in Oregon had these trees, they were worth over a million dollars in 1860.
Lloyd Rollins and his daughter Josephine arrived in Oregon and found gold as he had hoped. Mr. Rollins named the site Josephine County.

episodes.title: Galileo: The Great Man Whom No One Believed

subtitle.text: Imagine that you discovered something very important.
Imagine that your discovery was so important that it would change the way people think and live.
I'm sure that you would run out and tell everyone about your new discovery.
You might write a book about it and talk to many people.
Now imagine that no one believes you, and they even get angry with you.
They accuse you of being a liar and tell you that you are evil.
Finally, because you keep insisting that you are right, they throw you into prison for the rest of your life.
That is exactly what happened to Galileo Galilei.
Galileo was born in Pisa, which is a city in Italy, in 1564.
Galileo came from a well-respected family, and his parents expected him to become a doctor.
However, much to his father's disappointment, Galileo decided not to be a doctor.
He was more interested in mathematics and philosophy.
During his early years as a professor of mathematics, Galileo made some very important discoveries.
For instance, if you dropped a heavy ball and a light ball, which would hit the ground first?
Scientists used to think that the heavy ball would land first.
But Galileo believed they would hit the ground at the same time, and he wrote a mathematical formula to explain his idea.
To prove his theory, he climbed to the top of the famous Leaning Tower of Pisa and dropped two balls of the same size, one heavy and one light.
He proved his theory was correct. The two balls landed at the exact same time.
Because of this experiment, most people believed Galileo and accepted his new theory.
However, some people were not happy because Galileo's new ideas contradicted the old ones.
Sometimes new ideas make people feel uncomfortable and afraid.
Galileo's life took a drastic turn in 1609, when he heard about a new and incredible invention from the Netherlands.
It was a tool that made distant objects look near.
It was the telescope, and Galileo thought it was a fantastic invention.
Galileo began working on the telescope to make it more powerful.
He taught himself how to grind glass in order to make lenses for his telescope.
After many years and a lot of hard work, he made a telescope so powerful that it could magnify the stars and planets.
Before this, people could only view stars with their eyes.
Galileo's telescope impressed many people, and he became the highest-paid professor at his university.
Over the next few months, he made even more powerful telescopes.
This was when Galileo's real problems started.
At first he discovered some very interesting and wonderful things that no one questioned.
For example, he found that the moon was very bumpy instead of smooth.
He also discovered that Jupiter had four moons and that there were many more stars than people could see with the naked eye.
However, Galileo soon discovered something that made many people very angry.
By looking into space and observing the planets, the sun, and the stars,
he discovered that Earth was a ball that revolved around the sun like the other planets.
Many religious leaders thought that Galileo didn't believe in God and was questioning how the world was created.
They accused Galileo of doubting God's Word.
This was a big problem for Galileo because at that time, the Catholic Church was the most powerful organization in the world.
The religious leaders brought Galileo before the Inquisition.
The Inquisition was a religious court that decided if a person was saying things against the Christian faith.
If the judges decided that a person was speaking against God, they decided how to punish him.
The Inquisition decided that Galileo was against God, and his punishment was that he should not speak or write about his discoveries anymore.
But Galileo was a true scientist, and he did not want to be quiet.
So he continued to argue that his discoveries were not against the Bible and not against God.
He wanted people to hear what he was saying.
Once again Galileo was called before the Inquisition.
Now he was in very big trouble because this time he had disobeyed the Inquisition.
In order to stop Galileo from spreading his lies to other people, the Inquisition arrested him and imprisoned him for the rest of his life.
Of course, today we know that Galileo was right about many of his theories, and he has become one of the most respected thinkers of all time.
But at that time, he was the great man who no one believed.
"You did it, Wilbur," cried Orville as his brother landed their invention.
"Finally, we are successful. October the fifth of 1905 will go down in history," replied his brother.
"Today you flew the world’s first working airplane. You flew more than 24 miles.
This invention is really going to change the world," exclaimed Orville. "And we invented it!"
The Wright brothers were true inventors who spent their lives trying to build better machines.
Wilbur and Orville were extremely intelligent men.
Unlike most scientists, however, they did not go to a university. They were self-taught geniuses.
Wilbur was a fantastic student and was registered to attend Yale University.
But in 1886 he got hit in the face with a hockey stick.
The injury was so bad that it took him almost a year to recover.
By the time he recovered, his mother had become very sick.
So instead of going back to school, Wilbur spent the next year looking after his mother.
Whenever he had a spare moment, he would read.
During this time Orville also lost interest in school.
He found a part-time job in a small printing shop.
Orville knew that he could make a lot of money if he had a professional printing press, but it was far too expensive.
So together the two brothers built their own printing press.
They made it almost entirely from old junk that they found themselves, including a broken tombstone.
Soon their printing business was a success, so the brothers decided to build an even larger printing press.
Their second press was able to print one thousand sheets an hour, which was very fast at the time.
However, the Wright brothers were inventors and not printing men, and they soon became bored with the printing business.
In 1892 the Wright brothers became interested in a new sport: bicycle riding.
Because they were excellent mechanics, they soon had their own bicycle shop and became very good at fixing bicycles.
After a few years, Orville and Wilbur decided that they could build better bicycles than the ones they sold.
So they designed two bicycles that became very popular.
The Wright brothers were making a lot of money in the bicycle business, but making money was not what they liked best.
What they loved was to learn and invent.
During the next ten years, the Wright brothers would invent what almost everyone thought was impossible: the airplane. In
1896 Wilbur read a newspaper article about a famous German pilot who died flying a plane he had designed. From
that moment, he became very interested in the art of flying. After
careful thought, Wilbur and Orville guessed that the problem with the German pilot’s airplane was that it had no controls. Of
course, the Wright brothers thought they could design one that worked. The
first thing the Wright brothers did was to read everything that they could find on aviation. One
day while reading, Wilbur saw birds flying, and he noticed that they were constantly moving their wings to keep themselves balanced. This
was the big clue that he needed. The
Wright brothers decided to build a glider, that is, a plane with no engine. It
had wings that moved so that they could control and turn it. The
first two gliders that the Wright brothers built were not very successful. In
fact, the second one was so bad that Wilbur was almost killed trying to fly it. After
the crash, Wilbur said to his brother, "Not in a thousand years will man ever fly." However,
after being encouraged by other engineers, they decided to try again. In
1902, after careful research, the Wright brothers’ third glider was a success. Finally
they had built a plane that they could control. The
next step was to build an airplane with an engine, so that it could fly on its own power. The
brothers asked many engine companies to help them build an engine and propeller for their plane, but no one would help them. So
they decided to make their own engine and invented a method for making propellers. On
December 17, 1903, the Wright brothers’ first airplane was completed. The
Flyer made four very short flights, but then crashed and was completely destroyed. The
Wright brothers rebuilt the Flyer and called it the Flyer 2 . It worked but had many problems.
So in 1905, the Wrights completely rebuilt their aircraft.
The Flyer 3 was amazing. It was the first flying machine capable of taking off and flying through the air on its own power.
It could rise, descend, and turn in any direction that the pilot wanted.
Wilbur flew the plane over 24 miles and landed only when his plane ran out of gas.
It was an invention destined to change the world.
They come out onto the streets every year around Christmas time.
They are dressed in army-style uniforms, and they carry a bell and a red kettle.
People walking by often stop and put money into their kettles.
Who are these people with the red kettles? And why do people give them money?
They are members of the Salvation Army, which is a group of Christians who serve God by helping the poor.
Over one hundred years ago, William Booth, a Christian minister in London, England,
organized a small church group to help feed and provide housing for the poor.
As more and more people joined his group, William Booth decided to organize his church like an army.
Booth became the general of the army, and his ministers became the officers.
But unlike other armies that fight and kill people, Booth's army fought for God and the poor.
Many people were attracted to Booth's church because it was not very formal.
In Booth's church, people sang joyful songs, played instruments, and clapped their hands.
At his church, praising God was fun.
Also all people were treated equally and fairly in the Salvation Army.
It didn't matter if you were rich or poor, a man or a woman.
Catherine Booth, William Booth's wife, was also very involved in her husband's church.
She believed that women and men were equal in every way.
So in their church, the female members and the male members were all treated the same.
Many women were able to become officers in the Salvation Army.
Many Christians began to join the Salvation Army.
Soon the church services were full, and the Army was able to help the poor in great ways.
Before long, members of the Salvation Army started to spread out around the world.
Some officers went to Australia and others to America.
It was in America that one of these officers began the tradition of the Christmas kettle.
In 1891 Captain Joseph McFee decided that he wanted to provide a free Christmas dinner for the poor people in San Francisco.
However, he didn't have enough money to pay for it.
He spent several days thinking about how he was going to raise enough money for his dinner.
Then he came up with a great idea.
He remembered back to when he lived in Liverpool, England.
People in that city had a large pot that they put money into for the poor.
So the next day he got permission to set up a similar pot near the docks where the San Francisco ferry came in.
As people got on and off the ferry, they saw his pot and read a sign asking for donations.
He also put a smaller pot, called an urn, in the ferry waiting room.
It was a wonderful success. Captain McFee gathered enough money that Christmas to provide the poor people in San Francisco with a good Christmas dinner.
By 1895 the idea of Christmas kettles spread all across the west coast of the United States.
Soon the Salvation Army was preparing over thirty large Christmas dinners for thousands of poor people.
Then in 1897 a young officer named William McIntyre, who had helped Captain McFee start the Christmas kettle donations,
was sent to the east coast of the United States.
He wanted to bring the Christmas kettle tradition with him.
However, when he arrived in Boston, the other officers thought it was a strange idea and refused to help him.
But the poor people in Boston were very lucky because McIntyre didn't listen to the other officers.
McIntyre, his wife, and his sister went onto the streets of Boston with their kettles and began to raise money for a Christmas dinner for the poor.
That year over 150,000 poor people across the United States received a good Christmas dinner.
Over a hundred years later, the tradition of the Salvation Army Christmas dinner is stronger than ever.
The kettles are now used all over the world to help make Christmas better for unfortunate people.
In addition to helping the poor, the Salvation Army also provides dinners for elderly people without families,
sick people in hospitals, and even prisoners in jail.
Providing dinners for those who need them is not the only way the Salvation Army helps others.
In over eighty countries throughout the world, the people of the Salvation Army operate hospitals, schools, and homeless shelters.
They truly are God's soldiers.
These days their Christmas kettles look very different from the old pot that McFee used in San Francisco.
Some have fancy self-ringing bells, and others have speakers to play traditional Christmas carols.
However, they still announce the same message that "sharing is caring."
The Second World War was very hard on the people of Italy.
By the end of the war, some parts of Italy had been nearly destroyed from years of warfare.
Many people, especially the poor, could not see a future there for their families.
One of these people was a young man named Luigi.
Luigi was twenty years old, and he wanted to work, and buy a house for his family.
But jobs were scarce, and many homes around Italy had been demolished.
One day Luigi read an advertisement in the newspaper that told him about the American Dream.
"Come to America and you will find a job and a house," he read.
"In America everyone's dreams come true."
So Luigi packed his bags and kissed his wife and small baby boy good-bye.
"I will go to America and get a job.
Then you two can join me and we will buy a house and live a happy life," he said as he boarded the boat. "We will achieve the American Dream!"
When Luigi arrived in New York City, there were thousands of other men seeking the American Dream.
Luigi traveled from factory to factory, and construction site to construction site, looking for work.
But again and again employers rejected him.
Sometimes people were polite and apologized. "Sorry, no jobs today."
But other people treated him very rudely and shouted, "Scram, you dirty immigrant!
Go back to where you came from. We don't need immigrants around here."
Hungry, lonely, and depressed, Luigi took whatever jobs he could to make money.
For a few weeks, he shined shoes and worked as a sewer cleaner.
But these jobs didn't pay enough to bring over his wife and child, and the jobs were certainly not Luigi's idea of the American Dream.
Then Luigi heard about a small city with plenty of jobs and opportunities.
The city was Niagara Falls, and it was located about 11 hours from New York City.
So, with just a few pennies in his hand, Luigi boarded a train and headed north.
When he arrived in Niagara Falls, Luigi was amazed at how clean and beautiful it was.
"This is where I will find my American Dream," he declared.
Luigi began searching for a construction job.
But once again, everywhere he went, there were no jobs for immigrants.
Luigi grew desperate. He had absolutely no money, no friends, and no job.
Would he ever find the American Dream?
One morning he went to yet another construction site and asked for a job. The foreman said, "Sorry, nothing today."
Luigi became very angry and shouted, "I need a job, and I'm not leaving until I get one!"
With that, Luigi grabbed a shovel and started to work.
He began helping the construction workers dig a long and deep trench.
The astonished foreman watched in disbelief. "What are you doing?" he demanded.
"I'm working," replied Luigi. "If you don't like my work, you don't have to pay me.
But I'm working here today."
Luigi worked harder than any other man all day long.
At the end of the day, Luigi approached the foreman, "So do you like my work?"
"Yes, you do good work." The foreman acknowledged.
"Then I will come back tomorrow, and you will pay me," said Luigi.
At that all the other workmen started laughing.
They had never witnessed anything like this before.
"You are very bold," remarked one of the men.
"I'm not bold," retorted Luigi. "I'm just hungry."
The foreman smiled and said, "Okay, Luigi, you have a job. Come back tomorrow."
Then he reached into this pocket and pulled out some money.
"Here is your money for today. Go and get something to eat, and buy a new pair of boots."
After that Luigi worked every day. He was the first to arrive at the construction site in the morning and the last to leave at night.
Before long he had enough money for his wife and baby to come to America and join him.
Their house was located in an attractive Italian neighborhood in Niagara Falls.
Luigi and his wife eventually had more children.
After a few years, Luigi's family bought a new house that was bigger and very well constructed.
Their neighborhood was near good shops, safe schools, and a new church, which Luigi had helped to build.
His children attended school every day and grew up well.
Many years later Luigi went to the university to attend the graduation ceremony of his youngest son.
During the graduation ceremony, Luigi began to cry.
His wife looked at him in surprise. "Why are you crying?" she asked.
"They are tears of happiness," Luigi said.
"Today I have truly achieved the American Dream!"
Bonjour and welcome to France. This is the Palace of Versailles, and I am Andre Le Notre, the royal gardener.
I may not look like a gardener to you, but I designed all of the beautiful gardens around this palace.
In 1673 I helped make the beautiful gardens that you can still see in Versailles today.
Today only tourists and a few workers visit or live at the palace, but a great king once lived here.
He was King Louis XIV, who we call the Sun King.
By the time he died, Louis XIV had made Versailles one of the largest palaces in the world.
In 1623 Louis XIV's father, Louis XIII, built a small hunting lodge near the village of Versailles.
But Louis XIV loved Versailles so much that he had a grand palace built there.
In 1682 it became the official palace for the king of France.
Versailles has more than 2,000 windows, 700 rooms, 1,250 fireplaces, 67 staircases, and 50 fountains.
One of the most famous rooms is the Hall of Mirrors.
On the ceiling of this room, there are many paintings that depict the great life of Louis XIV.
Louis XIV was famous for more than just building nice gardens and decorating beautiful rooms.
He was a great king. Louis became king when he was only five years old.
Of course he could not rule France as a young boy, so his godfather and some noblemen were in charge of the country.
However, the noblemen did a very poor job of running the country, and the people of France became very unhappy with the royal family.
This made young King Louis very angry.
He wanted the people of France to be wealthy and happy because he loved his country.
But there was nothing he could do.
He had to wait until he grew up before he could become the ruler of France.
When he turned 23 years old, Louis XIV decided that it was time to govern the country himself.
None of the nobles believed it was possible for such a young king to rule a country. But he did.
He said, "I am the king! And the king is supreme."
Because he was so angry with the noblemen who had been running the country, he did not include them in his government.
Instead he chose the wisest and most loyal men he could find in France to help him. They became his ministers.
The young King Louis was a great success.
With his ministers, he helped the people of France prosper.
He developed factories and established trade with other countries.
He also supported many artists and scientists.
He and his ministers built a very powerful army.
Their army became the strongest force in all of Europe.
The French people became very proud of their country.
Life as a king was not easy for Louis XIV.
It was said that his days were planned right down to the minute, so he had almost no free time.
His days were filled with meetings and social gatherings.
All day long he went from one appointment to the next.
His first appointment usually began at eight thirty in the morning, and his last one ended around midnight.
King Louis was also a very religious man and went to church every day at ten o’clock in the morning.
He believed that as the king of France, he was God's servant on earth.
He built the Chapel Royal here at Versailles, which is one of the grandest parts of the castle.
Louis XIV is called the Sun King.
Louis wanted to be like the Greek god Apollo, who was the god of peace and arts.
The symbol for Apollo was the sun, so Louis also chose this as his emblem.
Louis XIV brought peace to France, developed the arts, and helped the people become wealthy.
Louis XIV died in 1715. He was king of France for 72 years, the longest reign in the history of Europe.
After Louis died, his son and then his grandson, Louis XV and Louis XVI, each became king.
But unlike Louis XIV, they were not great kings.
After a while the people of France became very unhappy with the royal family.
In 1793 they decided that they no longer wanted a king, so Louis XVI was arrested and killed.
Since that day France has had no king, and the Palace of Versailles has had no master.
In 1996 at the start of the twenty-sixth Olympic Games in Atlanta, Georgia, this great American hero lit the Olympic flame.
Who is this man? Why is he a great American hero?
These are difficult questions. To answer them we must go back over fifty years.
In 1942, when our hero was born, he was given the name Cassius Clay.
He was born into a poor, working-class, black family in Louisville, Kentucky.
When Cassius was a teenager, life for black families was very hard.
While white Americans were becoming rich, building nice houses, and going to good schools, black Americans were still very poor.
Cassius Clay never liked his name because it was a white man's name.
It was not a name that came from his ancestors, but rather it was the name of the slave owner who had owned his family years before.
As a child, Cassius Clay was furious with how white Americans treated black Americans.
When Cassius was 12, he started to box under the instructions of a policeman named Joe Martin.
Martin and others immediately saw that Cassius was a great boxer.
By the time he was 17, he had won a very important championship for young boxers: the Golden Gloves Championship.
Then in 1960, at the age of 18, Cassius went to the Olympics in Rome and won a gold medal.
He was on his way to becoming one of the greatest boxers in history.
After Cassius won a gold medal at the Olympics, he became a professional boxer.
His goal was to become the Heavyweight Champion of the World.
This is the highest title that a boxer can receive.
Cassius quickly became very famous. This was because he was not only a great boxer, but a good showman as well.
He would make up sayings about himself and other boxers.
His most famous line was: "I float like a butterfly and sting like a bee."
Cassius always said that he was the greatest boxer ever.
This made some people angry because he was so young and he had not yet fought the greatest boxers of the time.
But Cassius was a great boxer, and he had a new style of boxing.
On February 25, 1964, he fought Sonny Liston, the greatest boxer at that time, for the title of Heavyweight Champion of the World.
Of course everyone thought that Liston would easily win.
Cassius was called the underdog. That means everyone thought he was going to lose.
It was a very good fight. Both men fought hard for a long time.
Suddenly, to everyone's surprise, Cassius knocked out Liston and won the match, becoming the Heavyweight Champion of the World!
Two days later Cassius joined the Nation of Islam.
This is a group of black people who are committed to Allah and who take care of their bodies by not smoking, drinking, or acting immorally.
They also fight for a better life for black people in America.
At this time Cassius Clay gave up the slave name that he hated so much and chose a name based on his new religion.
Since then he has been called Muhammad Ali.
Muhammad Ali reached his goal and became the greatest boxer in the world.
Over the next three years, he fought in many matches and won every one of them.
He was truly the greatest fighter ever.
Then something very terrible happened to Muhammad Ali.
On April 28, 1967, Muhammad Ali was drafted into the United States Army to fight in the war in Vietnam.
However, he did not want to go to Vietnam because his religion taught him this war was not just.
Ali did not want to kill people who were not his enemies.
Because he refused to join the army, his title of Heavyweight Champion was taken away from him,
and he was not allowed to box anywhere in the United States.
Then on June 20, 1967, a formal trial was held by the government, and Ali was convicted of refusing to join the army.
He was sentenced to five years in prison.
During the late 1960s, Ali was very active in the Civil Rights Movement.
He encouraged black people to stand up against white people.
Finally in 1970 Ali was allowed to continue his boxing career.
Over the next ten years, Muhammad Ali proved that he truly was the greatest boxer in the world.
As Ali got older, he strengthened his religious beliefs.
He no longer hates white people like he did when he was young.
He believes that all people must work together to create a better world and prepare themselves for heaven.
Because Ali was a great boxer, he earned a lot of money.
However, he has shared his money with the poor.
He gave money to build schools, hospitals, and Islamic religious centers.
In 1981, after 22 years of boxing, Ali retired with one of the best records of all time.
In his career he competed in 61 fights. He won 56 of them and only lost 5.
A year after he retired, doctors discovered that Ali had an illness called Parkinson's disease.
Because of this disease, Ali is not able to speak well, and he moves very slowly.
However, his disease has not affected his mind. He still thinks very clearly.
To honor Muhammad Ali for his great contributions to sports and society,
he was chosen to light the Olympic flame at the start of the twenty-sixth Olympic games in Atlanta, Georgia.
And now you know why Muhammad Ali is a great American hero.
Hi, I’m Mary Chilton, and I am one of the original Pilgrims who survived a year of famine to celebrate the first Thanksgiving in the New World.
After arriving in the New World, the first thing we needed to do was to write a document that would guide our new society.
The men gathered together and wrote the Mayflower Compact.
Every man who had traveled aboard the Mayflower signed the agreement on November 21, 1620.
Soon after the Mayflower Compact was signed, the men went exploring to find a place where we could build our new homes.
After several days they returned to the Mayflower with some corn they had found.
"We think we will find a place to settle soon," they told us hopefully.
We were relieved. "Oh, thank the Lord," we said.
After six more weeks of exploration, our men sent word that they had found a place to settle.
December 31, 1620, was our first chance to see the place we would call home. We named it Plymouth.
The weather in January was bad, but the men worked hard to cut logs for the settlement.
First, they built a common house to store our tools, furnishings, and supplies. Then, they built houses.
The work went slowly because many people were ill, and more than half died in the Great Sickness that winter.
My family was one of the hardest hit. I lost both my father and my mother.
My father was the oldest Pilgrim to make the voyage to the New World, and he died very quickly.
My mother was a very strong woman, but she also died.
I know in my heart that she died because she wanted me to live.
She always made sure I ate first.
She would give me some of her food because there wasn’t really enough food for all of us to eat.
By the end of the winter, more than half of those who had crossed on the Mayflower had died, but the older women were the hardest hit.
Only 5 of the 18 original married women aboard the Mayflower survived.
Although I was now an orphan with no mother or father, the other Pilgrims took me in and treated me with kindness.
With so many women dead, I found myself busier than ever.
I had to help do the cooking and the laundry for the men and boys who had lost their wives and mothers.
In March of 1621, a Native American came to our village.
His name was Samoset. He walked into the village shouting, "Welcome! Welcome, Englishmen!"
Even though it was a very cold and windy day, Samoset was naked except for a cloth around his waist and moccasins on his feet.
The men talked to Samoset for a long time.
Samoset left the next day after promising to return soon.
After several days Samoset did return with another Native American who amazed us all with his flawless English.
His name was Squanto, and he said he was the last surviving member of the Patuxet tribe.
Squanto stayed with us that whole spring and summer.
He taught our men how to hunt and how to fish.
He taught the women how to plant and cultivate corn, squash, and beans.
Squanto helped us to make friends with the neighboring tribes.
With his help, we signed a peace treaty with King Massasoit.
We learned that our seeds from England did not grow very well in the New World,
but Squanto showed us that if we planted our seeds with herring, then they would grow.
Squanto and other Native Americans also helped us with our crops.
With their help, our corn, squash, and beans did very well that year.
To celebrate our bountiful harvest, we invited the great King Massasoit and his advisors to our village.
The feast lasted for three days. We ate duck, turkey, deer, clams, lobster, and many kinds of fish.
There were lots of berries, nuts, and several kinds of fruit.
But the best dish of all was an Indian pudding made from pumpkin and sweetened with the syrup from a maple tree.
We thanked God for the success of our harvest and for the kindness of the Native Americans who taught us the skills we needed to survive.
This is the story of Amelia Earhart.
She was an airplane pilot and a great American hero.
On July 2, 1937, the airplane that Amelia Earhart was flying crashed near Howland Island in the Pacific Ocean.
For many months people searched for Amelia Earhart's plane, but it was never found.
Since 1937 there have been many other expeditions to find Amelia's plane, but no one has been able to find it.
Amelia Earhart was born on July 24, 1897, to Amy and Edwin Earhart.
She was born in Kansas City, but lived all over the United States.
When she was ten, her family moved to Iowa. Amelia began keeping a diary.
July 1908: "Today is my tenth birthday.
It was a great day. Father took us to the Iowa State Fair.
It was very exciting. I saw an airplane for the first time.
It was a strange-looking thing, and I can't imagine anyone flying in it."
In 1917, during World War I, Amelia went to visit her sister at school in Canada.
While she was there, she decided to train as a nurse.
She served as a volunteer at a military hospital in Toronto and helped heal many soldiers until the war ended in 1918.
November 1918: "The war has finally ended, and I am going back to the United States.
It was a terrible war. I tried to help as many soldiers as I could, but many men died.
I hope there is never another war."
After the war Amelia went to California to be with her mother and father.
It was in California that Amelia fell in love with flying.
December 1920: "A few days ago, I had the most exhilarating day of my life.
I went with Father to Daugherty Field.
We watched an air show. Today I got a chance to fly in an airplane, and I loved it! I have to fly again."
January 1921: "I met Neta today. She is going to give me flying lessons.
I am going to become an airplane pilot!"
March 1921: "This was the worst day of my life.
I had another accident in my airplane.
Neta thinks that I may never be a good pilot.
Mother and Father agree with her and want me to stop flying.
But I will never stop. Flying is my life now.
I will show them that I can be a great pilot.
I will become the best pilot ever."
June 1921: "Today I bought an airplane and named it the Canary.
Unfortunately I got into a very small accident when I was landing the plane. But tomorrow will be better."
Amelia never gave up. She worked very hard for the next seven years and became an excellent pilot.
During those seven years, she also became famous.
In fact, the Boston Globe called her the best woman pilot in the United States.
April 1928: "I am so excited. Today I got a call from Captain Railey.
He asked me to become the first woman to fly across the Atlantic Ocean.
I will be the captain of the flight, and two men will come with me.
But my dream is to fly across the Atlantic Ocean by myself."
May 1932: "I did it! I flew across the Atlantic by myself.
It was not easy, but I persisted. I encountered a thunderstorm and heavy fog.
All I had to eat on the trip was two cans of tomato juice.
I had hoped to land in Paris, France, but because of the storm, I landed in Ireland."
June 1932: "What a day! First, there was a parade for me in New York City.
Thousands of people came out onto the street to cheer for me.
I felt like a hero. Later I flew to Washington DC and went to the White House.
President Hoover presented me with an award."
After her solo Atlantic flight, Amelia was very famous.
Her next goal was to fly around the world.
December 1936: "I have decided to fly all the way around the world.
I will be the first woman to do it. But even more important, I will fly around the world at the equator.
If I succeed, it will be the longest distance ever traveled in one airplane trip.
Not even any man has flown so far.
The trip will need careful planning and preparation.
I will have to do a trial flight to test equipment, and I’ll have to carefully research the best route."
May 1937: "I said good-bye to my friends, my family, and many of my new fans today.
I have begun my journey around the world.
It will take about a month. Today I flew from California and I will land in Florida in a few days."
During her long trip, Amelia continued writing her diary.
Whenever she landed, she found a way to send her diary entries home to her husband, George Putnam.
Her last entry was in July 1937. It was very short.
"Tomorrow I will be flying over Howland Island. I hope it is a nice day."
Then, the very next day, her plane crashed near Howland Island.
Immediately searchers went out to find her.
President Roosevelt sent 9 Navy ships and 66 airplanes.
They searched for almost a month, but could not find her.
Still to this day, no one has been able to find her plane.
Amelia Earhart was a courageous and brave woman.
Before she left on her flight around the world, Amelia wrote this letter to her husband:
Dear George,
Please know I am aware that this trip will be dangerous, but I must make it.
Women must try to do the things that men have done.
Even if I fail, I hope that my adventure will challenge other women to try.
My name is Mary Chilton. I am one of the original Pilgrims to set sail for the New World in a ship called the Mayflower
. A Pilgrim is a person who makes a journey for a religious
reason. The story of the Pilgrims begins in
Holland. Even though I am English, I was born in Leyden, Holland, in
1607. My family lived in Holland because we were not free to practice our religion in England, but Holland wasn't our home.
It was a strange and foreign land.
I lived there with my parents for 12 years.
In 1619 we returned to England to prepare for a voyage to the New World.
My parents and many other adults packed trunks and barrels with all the things we would need to begin life in the New World.
They hired two ships, the Mayflower and the Speedwell , to take us to the New
World. We were all very excited and a little
scared. We left England on August 5, 1620, but we had to return to England because the Speedwell was
leaking. We tried to fix the ship, but it was too old and
tired. We were forced to abandon it, leaving behind our cooking oil and some other valuables. We all piled into the
Mayflower . We finally set sail for the New World on September
6, 1620. There were 130 people aboard
the Mayflower . There were 102 Pilgrims and about 28 crew members. Three of the women
were pregnant! It took us 66 days to reach the
New World. Many of us became seasick when the Mayflower was tossed around by storms and
strong waves. I spent many days being sick below deck because going above deck
was dangerous. The wind, rain, and waves made the deck slippery, so it was easy to
fall overboard. When it wasn't stormy and scary, the voyage
was boring. At home I was never bored because I was busy helping my mother with the sewing, the laundry, or
the cooking. But, on the Mayflower , there was very little women's work that needed
to be done. I could have died, not from seasickness,
but from boredom. Luckily, I had two friends, Constance Hopkins
and Elizabeth Tilley. They made me laugh
with their stories. Elizabeth was in love with John Howland, but he took no
notice of her. It was both funny and sad, but never boring to watch her
unrequited love. When we weren't listening to Elizabeth, we were often trying to avoid
Francis Billington. He was a bully who liked to pull our hair. He was such
a troublemaker! Once, he started a fire on board the Mayflower when he shot his father's gun
below deck. Luckily, everyone heard the sound and put the
fire out. The scariest moment aboard the Mayflower was when the ship was caught in a terrible storm for two
whole days. In the single room below deck where we all lived, we huddled together and prayed to God to
save us. We weren't sure that God was listening, however, because on the second day of the storm, one of the main beams below
deck cracked. Many of the sailors were scared because they knew that the ship couldn't survive
another storm. The passengers also feared they would die. But God was
merciful. No other storms caught us, and only two men died on the
voyage. On November 9, 1620, we finally saw
land. The ship's captain called the place Cape Cod, and he said it was many miles north of
Virginia. We were all glad to see land after having spent 66 days in a small room with 102 seasick
people. We were also looking forward to breathing fresh air because the Mayflower smelled most
unpleasant! On November 13, 1620, I was the first woman to step off of the Mayflower into the New
World. I went ashore to help with the
laundry. It was the only time in my life I was ever thankful to God for making laundry women's work, because it allowed me to stand firmly on the
ground. We wanted to continue south to Virginia because there were other Englishmen who had settled there, but our attempt to sail south failed.
The ship didn't dare go far from shore because of the damage to the beam.
So we decided to remain in Cape Cod.
We sent the men out to explore, and on December 12, 1620, the men returned.
They had found a suitable place. They had also made contact with Native Americans.
On December 15, 1620, we went ashore and started our new life in the New World.
It wouldn't be an easy life, but we were hopeful.
